Name: Katie Cornine
Badge: Everyday Sparks
Which strategy from this module (Writer’s Notebook, Quicklists, or Writing Sprints) feels most immediately usable in your teaching context? Why?:

I plan to use all 3 strategies in this module because they are quick. I am a Title 1 teacher who does small reading intervention groups. These activities could be easily implemented as a warm-up before my intervention lessons. I like that these activities are low stakes too.

What do you anticipate will be the biggest challenge in bringing daily writing into your classroom, and how might you address it?:

Time! I have 20-30 minutes for each intervention group. I need to cover the missing skills. I plan to use these strategies as a warm-up. Through these modules, I am concluding that I need to connect writing to reading. I think on the first day of implementation, we will introduce the writer's notebook and create the quick lists. I think I will do this along with my students. I will use a timer so we can complete in under 5 minutes. On the 2nd day of implementation, I will be able to have students do the writing sprints. I love that these activities are quick and low stakes. I will be able to get a lot of information from students' writing samples that will help me with my intervention lessons. Misspellings will draw my attention to missing phonics skills or morphological elements rules that need to be retaught. I have attached posters created on Canva that I plan to display during the implementation of these activities. I plan on students writing directly in their writer's notebooks. My internet is slow at home. Can you let me know if the file uploaded correctly? Thanks.
